title: QCOEM: Quantum Cloud Orchestration with Evolutionary Multi-Objective Optimization
authors: Tam N. Pham, Hoa T. Nguyen, Quan Le-Trung
abstract: Quantum cloud platforms need to dynamically orchestrate workloads across heterogeneous quantum computation backends whose noise profiles, qubit topologies, and queues vary over time. Existing orchestrators use noise-agnostic heuristics that ignore backend-specific errors, causing reduced execution fidelity, load imbalance, and frequent rescheduling. To address these challenges, we propose QCOEM - a Quantum Cloud Orchestration framework that leverages Evolutionary algorithms for Multi-objective optimization of quantum task scheduling. We compare NSGA-II and NSGA-III for jointly minimizing mean completion time, execution error rate, and load imbalance. To select schedules from a non-convex Pareto front, we apply an Augmented Achievement Scalarization Function (AASF) as a preference-based decision rule that maps the Pareto set to a single dispatchable schedule aligned with user priorities. Our extensive performance evaluation in a heterogeneous quantum cloud environment shows zero task rescheduling and about 30% higher mean fidelity than noise-agnostic heuristics, while maintaining bounded scheduling overhead. The experiment results indicate that our QCOEM framework can deliver stable, high-fidelity execution and lightweight resource management for quantum cloud computing.
summary: This paper introduces QCOEM, a framework that uses multi-objective evolutionary optimization to schedule quantum tasks across noisy, heterogeneous cloud hardware. By jointly optimizing mean completion time, error rate, and load balance, it significantly outperforms simple heuristics. This work provides a crucial tool for achieving stable, high-fidelity execution in practical quantum cloud computing settings.
main_problem: Dynamically orchestrating quantum workloads across heterogeneous cloud backends while managing time-varying noise profiles, qubit topologies, and queue congestion.
main_result: The QCOEM framework achieves about 30% higher mean fidelity than noise-agnostic heuristics and eliminates task rescheduling in a simulated environment.
method: It formulates the problem as a Multi-Objective Optimization Problem (MOOP) solved using NSGA-II/III, followed by preference selection via an Augmented Achievement Scalarization Function (AASF).
model_or_system: The system models a heterogeneous quantum cloud environment composed of multiple Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era Quantum Processing Units (QPUs), managed via a centralized scheduler.
key_observables: Mean Task Completion Time, Mean Error Rate (Fidelity), Load Imbalance (standard deviation of completion times), and Scheduling Overhead.
important_parameters: Calibrated hardware snapshots (error rates, coupling maps), user priority weights ($w$), and batch sizes ($M$).
main_assumptions: The problem is NP-hard, necessitating heuristic approximation via MOEAs; it assumes stable hardware snapshots and FIFO queueing on QNodes.
figures_summary: Figures compare performance across different optimization objectives (Load-Focus vs. Quality-Focus) against baseline heuristics, illustrating trade-offs between time efficiency, fidelity, and task distribution.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the QCOEM framework architecture, details the MOOP formulation with three objectives, presents the use of NSGA-II/III for Pareto front approximation, and concludes with extensive performance evaluation comparing its results against classical scheduling methods.
why_interesting: While focused on cloud orchestration rather than fundamental physics, the core challenge involves optimizing complex resource allocation under realistic noise constraints, which has implications for designing robust quantum control protocols or understanding system-level decoherence effects in large arrays of qubits.
